unusual_experiment.name: amputated launch with zero sidecars
unusual_experiment.intervention: Copy only EntityOS into an otherwise empty temporary directory and run its self-test.
unusual_experiment.baseline: Same exact EntityOS self-test in exact-head checkout.
unusual_experiment.rollback: Delete temporary directory; no persistent runtime state modified.
unusual_experiment.interpretation: The tested compiler/parser/VM/ClayOS/Linux-process smoke path no longer requires repository sidecars or host site-packages beyond the Python interpreter/host OS boundary.

counterevidence: Whole Clay Machine acceptance remains false: canonical Bytes/Buffer ownership/lifetime, String/argv/effectful TypedIR/VM process path, network, visual, audio, portability and self-hosting gates remain open.
Single-file packaging success is not proof that all included modules are semantically complete or exercised.

grf_collapse.preferred_reality: A zipapp-style single-file boundary can carry the current ClayCode parser/compiler path, one ClayVM, ClayEnv/ClayOS surface and controlled Linux process smoke when runtime dependency closure and archive-hostile resources are explicitly captured.
grf_collapse.counter_reality_rejected: Current Clay Machine source necessarily requires a multi-file runtime merely to execute the admitted smoke path.
grf_collapse.promotion: PROMOTE_TO_VERIFIED for the exact single-file smoke boundary only; NOT whole-machine acceptance.

next_discriminator: Advance the canonical semantic frontier rather than packaging breadth: select the smallest Clay Bytes/Buffer ownership+lifetime plus String/argv/effect-signature surface and route one provenance-bound opaque-byte/process request through canonical checker -> effectful ExecutableTypedIR -> single ClayVM -> ClayOS Linux boundary without backend-local semantics.
